shouldFix.title: fromVnCheck and honestyRepairsKeyRule state incompatible scopes, and the register currently fails fromVnCheck on two v6/v7 BLOCKER findings whose stated consequence is that the successor refuses
evidence: The two GOVERNING rules disagree on scope. registerCoverageRule.fromVnCheck reads, with no version bound, 'every register finding whose disposition is REPAIRED MUST appear as a fromVnIdExtractionRule result for honestyRepairsFromV[0-9]+ after findingIdRule validation'. honestyRepairsKeyRule reads 'Every REPAIRED finding id in predecessorVerdictFindings for v8 onward MUST appear in honestyRepairsFromVN', and separately that the register 'is maintained from v6 onward'.

Two live findings sit in the gap. predecessorVerdictFindings.v6.codex records HAE6-CX-01 with severity BLOCKER and disposition REPAIRED, and v7.codex records HAE7-CX-01 with severity BLOCKER and disposition REPAIRED. Enumerating every repair-array prefix, the arrays run honestyRepairsFromV9 through honestyRepairsFromV21; there is no honestyRepairsFromV6 or honestyRepairsFromV7 and neither id appears anywhere in them. Scanning all sixteen register rounds, these two are the only REPAIRED findings with no repair-array entry.
So the register does not merely permit a violation of fromVnCheck as written; it exhibits one today, on two BLOCKER-severity findings.

The stated consequence is not advisory. registerCoverageRule.resultIfIncomplete reads 'the successor refuses; do not claim REPAIRED for a coverage finding', and enforcement reads 'authoring a successor includes the per-lane (id, severity) frozen-review coverage check'. An author applying registerCoverageRule literally would refuse to author v22.

The scope conflict became reachable only this generation, which is why no earlier round caught it. registerCoverageRule.when carries no lower bound, but until v21 nothing exercised the v6 and v7 entries: I ran every corpus verification from v8 through v20 because the FromVN obligation is scoped v8 onward, and the legacy-exemption repair in v22 is the first clause to name v6 and v7 lanes explicitly.

The intended reading is not in doubt, which is what bounds the severity. honestyRepairsKeyRule's v8-onward sentence is specific and deliberate, the repair arrays have started at V9 for their entire history, and v8 itself carries no findings, so the exemption was always meant to cover exactly v6 and v7. Only fromVnCheck's wording fails to say so.
shouldFix.impact: registerCoverageRule is the artifact's mechanical gate on successor authoring and it is offered as GOVERNING, so a clause that the current register cannot satisfy makes the gate unusable as written: an implementer either refuses to author any successor, or silently substitutes the other rule's scope and thereby stops applying the check as stated. Both outcomes defeat the purpose of a mechanical check, and the second is the more likely and the more damaging, because it establishes that the stated text is not what is actually run. That is the same failure mode as the v16 defect where a rule's stated obligation and the artifact's practice diverged, and it undermines every coverage assurance the register is meant to provide.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Give fromVnCheck the same explicit scope its sibling rule already carries, so that it reads every register finding whose disposition is REPAIRED for v8 onward. If instead the v6 and v7 findings are meant to be covered, add honestyRepairsFromV6 and honestyRepairsFromV7 arrays carrying HAE6-CX-01 and HAE7-CX-01 and drop the v8-onward bound from honestyRepairsKeyRule. Either resolution is acceptable; what is not is two GOVERNING rules stating different scopes for the same obligation while the register satisfies only one of them.

advisories.observation: Partitioning the v21 to v22 leaf diff, zero substantive paths changed and nothing was removed anywhere; the only GOVERNING addition is legacyVerdictOnlyReviews. The same holds for every generation since v13. The authorization content itself, failClosed's six conjuncts, coveredActs and its class gates, the authorizationRecord schema and its 19-member mapping, effectCommit, outcomeVocabulary and joinBlockerDisposition, is unchanged, and BLK-1 through BLK-4 remain STILL-ROUTED. The artifact has grown from 71101 bytes at recorded v8 to 138440 bytes, with essentially all of that growth in the machinery that governs its own review.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: This is an observation about where review effort has gone, not a defect in the artifact. Every bookkeeping finding across these ten generations has been real, including three of mine and eight of Codex's, and the substantive content was independently examined and found coherent at v16 and v19. Nothing has regressed. I record it a second time, and more precisely, because the trend is now unambiguous and because a coordinator weighing whether this candidate is converging on DR-105 and DR-114 should have the measurement rather than the impression.

measurements.legacyAllowlistDetail: Rather than check the list against my own requiredRepair, I re-derived the qualifying set from the pinned files: reading both status members from all thirty-two lane files gives exactly eight with both absent. The allowlist has exactly eight entries and the two sets are in bijection, with no statusless lane missing from the list and no listed path that is not statusless or not in the register. Every listed digest reproduces against its file, and every listed verdict agrees with both the file's verdict field and the register entry's. terminalStatusCheck is now keyed on identity rather than absence, stating that a file with both status members absent whose digest is not on the list REFUSES, which is the repair my finding and Codex's both required.
measurements.newClausesProbedDetail: Per my stub commitment I probed the new constraints as hard as the repaired one. Fifteen probes, all behaving correctly. verdictEligibility refuses PENDING, lowercase accept, ACCEPT with a trailing space, a boolean and a number, so the vocabulary is closed on both type and value. The biconditional refuses ACCEPT carrying a SHOULD-FIX and refuses REJECT carrying only advisories, while admitting ACCEPT with only advisories and REJECT with a blocker. terminalStatusCheck refuses a statusless file absent from the allowlist, refuses an allowlist path presented with a wrong digest, refuses IN-PROGRESS in either status member, and admits both COMPLETE and COMPLETED. laneCheck also now states the order of operations explicitly, provenanceCheck then terminalStatusCheck then verdictEligibility then extraction, which removes the question of whether the digest is verified before the file is read.

Every path exists, every recorded digest reproduces, every recorded verdict equals its pinned file's verdict, every terminal-eligibility test passes by allowlist or by COMPLETE status, and every lane's (id, severity) set equals its extracted set. The v21 round is registered for both lanes with correct severities and dispositions.

It does not mark DR-105 or DR-114 SATISFIED, does not seal, does not bind, does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/, does not mint or imply a D-096 (A) grant, does not retarget D-093 or recorded v8, does not edit the subject, does not edit file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, does not edit any frozen v4-v21 verdict, and does not commit. It writes exactly one file, this one.
verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. The claimed repair is complete and I verified it without relying on its resemblance to my own wording: re-deriving the qualifying set from the pinned files gives exactly the eight statusless lanes the allowlist names, in bijection, with every digest reproducing, and eligibility is now keyed on identity rather than absence. The new constraints were probed as hard as the repaired one, fifteen probes covering the closed verdict vocabulary on type and value and the severity biconditional in both directions, all behaving correctly, and the full corpus from v6 through v21 passes every stated check with zero failures. The finding is a scope conflict between two GOVERNING rules that this generation is the first to make reachable. fromVnCheck requires every REPAIRED register finding to have a repair-array entry with no version bound, while honestyRepairsKeyRule bounds the same obligation to v8 onward; HAE6-CX-01 and HAE7-CX-01, both BLOCKER and both REPAIRED, have no entry and no arrays exist for those rounds. The register therefore fails fromVnCheck as written today, and that clause's stated consequence is that the successor refuses. I bounded it at SHOULD-FIX because the intended scope is unambiguous from the sibling rule and no authorization semantics are touched. I record that this became visible only because my own v21 finding established that v6 and v7 are governed, and that through v20 I ran every verification from v8 and would not have seen it.
